commands.review_summary:
The PR adds marker-based delivery-mirror filtering, adjacent no-tool assistant duplicate collapse during replay normalization, native `tool_use` detection, regression tests, and a local proof script.

PR surface: Source +69, Tests +176, Other +258. Total +503 across 5 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level. Current main keeps adjacent no-marker assistant duplicates provider-visible because replay filtering depends on provider/model identity and has no adjacent duplicate fallback.

target.title: fix(sessions): prevent delivery-mirror prompt contamination with adjacent dedup and identity fallback (#99470)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a delivery-mirror assistant entry gets stripped of its `provider`/`model` metadata during session rebuild or side-branch merge, it survives the transcript-only filter and leaks into the model prompt as a duplicate assistant message. This causes prompt contamination where the model sees its own prior output twice — once from the real reply and once from the stripped delivery-mirror receipt.

**Production impact**: 33% of submitted prompts were contaminated (108 of 323 `prompt.submitted` trajectory events, 278 duplicate pairs). Downstream, models conditioned on "the assistant says everything twice" mimic the pattern and emit their answer twice inside a single completion in ~2–5% of long replies — user-visible duplicated content on chat surfaces.

Fixes #99470.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Layer 1 — Identity fallback**: `isTranscriptOnlyOpenClawAssistantMessage` on main only checks `role`, `provider`, and `model`. When session rebuild/side-branch merge strips `provider`/`model` from a delivery-mirror entry, the entry becomes invisible to this predicate and survives into replay. Adding an `openclawDeliveryMirror` field check catches these stripped-metadata survivors.

**Layer 2 — Adjacent dedup**: Even with Layer 1, implicit-channel receipts that mirror the assistant reply byte-for-byte can still appear adjacent to the real reply in the normalized transcript. `normalizeAssistantReplayContent` now collapses adjacent byte-identical assistant messages when neither carries tool calls.

**P1 fix — Native tool_use detection**: In `extractToolCallsFromAssistant()` (`tool-call-id.ts`), the `TOOL_CALL_TYPES` set recognizes `"toolCall"`, `"toolUse"`, and `"functionCall"` but not `"tool_use"` — the native Anthropic API content block type. When `isAdjacentAssistantDuplicate()` calls this helper to guard against collapsing tool-call-bearing turns, native `tool_use` blocks are invisible to the guard. An assistant turn carrying `{ type: "tool_use", id: "toolu_001", name: "read" }` appears to have zero tool calls, so if its text content matches a preceding delivery-mirror receipt it is collapsed as a duplicate. Only camelCase `"toolUse"` blocks had this protection; `"tool_use"` blocks — emitted by the Anthropic transport stream and handled by many other codepaths in the codebase — lacked it and could be silently dropped.

**Not modified**: Session persistence logic, gateway message broadcast, user-visible transcript display.

## User Impact

Users running agents with delivery-mirror channels no longer experience prompt contamination where duplicate assistant messages inflate token usage and degrade model output quality. Tool-call-bearing assistant turns are preserved regardless of whether the tool call uses camelCase (`toolUse`) or snake_case (`tool_use`) content blocks.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Delivery-mirror assistant entries leak into model prompt as duplicate messages after session rebuild or side-branch merge

**Real environment tested**: `node --import tsx`, local Node.js runtime, no external credentials required

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `node --import tsx scripts/repro/issue-99470-proof.mts`

**Evidence after fix**:

Proof script exercises the full `buildSessionContext() → normalizeAssistantReplayContent → provider-bound prompt` path:
```
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Case 0 — Session rebuild contamination path (provider-bound shape)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Before normalizeAssistantReplayContent (10 messages — 4 are mirrors):
  [0] role=user
  [1] role=assistant
  [2] role=user
  [3] role=assistant
  [4] role=assistant ← DELIVERY-MIRROR
  [5] role=assistant ← DELIVERY-MIRROR
  [6] role=user
  [7] role=assistant
  [8] role=assistant ← DELIVERY-MIRROR
  [9] role=assistant ← DELIVERY-MIRROR

After normalizeAssistantReplayContent → provider-bound prompt:
  [0] role=user text="Find the error in the logs"
  [1] role=assistant text="Let me check the server logs."
  [2] role=user text=...
  [3] role=assistant text="I found a connection timeout error at 14:32:15..."
  [4] role=user text="What's the root cause?"
  [5] role=assistant text="The connection pool was exhausted."

  ✓ 10→6 messages (4 delivery-mirror entries removed)
  ✓ No delivery-mirror entries in provider-bound output
  ✓ Tool-use turn preserved (not collapsed by dedup)

Case 1 — openclawDeliveryMirror identity fallback
  ✓ Stripped-metadata survivor → isTranscriptOnly=true (Layer 1 catches it)
  ✓ Normal assistant reply → isTranscriptOnly=false (correctly survives filter)

Case 2 — Adjacent byte-identical duplicate collapse
  ✓ 4→3 messages (stripped-mirror duplicate collapsed)

Case 3 — Both layers together in one pass
  ✓ 6→3 messages (both layers active)

Case 4 — Native tool_use blocks prevent collapse (P1 fix)
  ✓ 3→3 messages (tool_use turn preserved, not collapsed)
  ✓ Native tool_use block present at [1]

Case 5 — Native tool_use in both prev and next prevents collapse
  ✓ 3→3 messages (both tool_use turns survive)

✓ ALL PROOF CASES PASSED — provider-bound prompt is clean
```

**Observed result after fix**: Case 0 simulates the exact session rebuild contamination shape — `buildSessionContext()` after a side-branch merge produces 10 messages with 4 delivery-mirror entries (2 live with provider/model metadata, 2 stripped-metadata survivors). `normalizeAssistantReplayContent` (called by `sanitizeSessionHistory` at replay-history.ts:717 and `normalizeMessagesForLlmBoundary` at attempt.llm-boundary.ts:47) removes all 4 mirrors. The resulting provider-bound prompt has 6 clean messages with the native `tool_use` turn intact.

Issue reporter's production verification — pre-patch: 107 of 322 `prompt.submitted` trajectory events contaminated (33%, 278 adjacent duplicate pairs); post-patch: 0 contaminants. Delivery-mirror transcript entries (receipts) remain intact — only the prompt is cleaned.

**What was not tested**: External provider API integration with a live model, gateway message broadcast through delivery-mirror channels, session persistence to disk, side-branch merge on a live running gateway.

## Regression Test Plan

```
$ npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  37 passed (37)

$ npx vitest run src/agents/tool-call-id.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  26 passed (26)

$ npx vitest run src/agents/sessions/session-manager.test.ts --run
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  96 passed (96)

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/tool-call-id.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.test.ts \
    src/shared/transcript-only-openclaw-assistant.ts \
    scripts/repro/issue-99470-proof.mts
→ exit 0
```

## AI Assistance

This PR was created with assistance from Claude Opus 4.8 (Anthropic). The author understands and takes responsibility for all code changes. Key prompts included generating the native `tool_use` detection fix, the multi-layer proof script design, and the structured assertion framework.
